notes: The board is one story: a global risk-off session, not a stock-picking day. Reuters (11/20 01:46 UTC) has the S&P 500 down 2.02%, the Dow down 2.19% and the Nasdaq down 2.25% on 11/19 — a sixth straight down session for the index — with a global equity gauge on its seventh straight decline and Asian shares heading for their worst week since 2020. The macro overlay is rates: the Philly Fed prices index at its highest since April, the 10-year near 5.05%, and traders pricing roughly a 95% chance of a December rate HIKE. Gold fell about 2.7%.

The dominant structural driver is the AI-infrastructure unwind, which travelled down the supply chain — optical -> foundry -> memory -> accelerator -> AI cloud — and it is one story across many tickers, not a series of company events: AAOI, COHR, LITE, CRDO, MXL, BE, SNDK, AXTI, AMD, MRVL, DELL, NBIS, ONDS and ASTS all moved on the same hyperscaler-capex-and-returns repricing. The engine classifies most of them IDIOSYNCRATIC because the sector ETFs were down less than 1.5pp; that is a mechanical artefact of the proxy rule, and the context is a single sector-wide de-rating.

The Anthropic IPO is the day's headline and the market's test case: it priced at $83, opened at $111.50 and closed at $97.17 (+17%) on 11/19, then gave the gain back pre-market on 11/20. Reuters frames it as the debut failing to restore faith in the AI sector. ANT is a one-day-old IPO with no earnings anchor, so its gap is a sentiment print, not a valuation print.

Two session-specific catalysts sit on top of that backdrop: Intuit reported after the close on 11/19 and guided Q2 below consensus while selling Mailchimp, and BJ's reported before the open on 11/20, beat, raised guidance and was still sold. BJ is the cleanest read that this tape is being sold on any good news at all.

Crypto is a beta leg, not an independent driver: bitcoin was around $61,300-61,800 in the early hours, its lowest since early July, with crypto market capitalisation back near mid-summer lows. PURR, WULF and CYPH in the ladder are tracking that, and the engine's crypto proxy was unavailable this run, so those names carry a proxy-free driver class.

Focus-book context: the 2026-11-19 sweep's Focus list is a momentum book built on 11/19, so it structurally cannot hold the day's real gappers. Every Focus name this morning is gapping DOWN with the market — the screen's setups are being sold with the tape, not against it. NUAI is the only Focus name that touched the 4% bar, and it is a reversal of its own PPA-driven run rather than a fresh setup.

The one decision that moved during this run is NUAI's, and the reason is size, not direction. Wave 1 (08:35:55 ET) carried a 90-share print behind the gap and it cleared the flag gate; waves 2 and 3 found newer prints at the same price level but on 23 shares and then 1 share, so the final tape lands the name on BORDERLINE_THIN. The gap itself never moved off the bar and the pre-market volume is real, so this is a thin-print verdict on a wide gap, not a name that stopped moving. A reader should treat NUAI as a genuine wide mover whose SNAPSHOT print is not tradeable, and re-check the tape after the open.

The pre-market tape is drying out as the session ages: the newest prints on the decision-relevant names are getting smaller across the three waves, and the names are drifting further below their pre-market highs. The 4% bar therefore looks staler with every wave, not fresher.
